notes: Identity independently verified from supplied text: matching title Young Adults’ Fertility Expectations and Events: Associations With College Enrollment and Persistence; authors R Kelly Raley, Yujin Kim, Kimberly Daniels; J Marriage Fam. 2012 Aug;74(4):866–879; DOI 10.1111/j.1741-3737.2012.00990.x; PMCID PMC3665345. PMC author-manuscript full primary report with Method, Results, Tables 1–5, Discussion and references; not an abstract-only or secondary article. No PDF supplied, so printed page 8 cannot be mapped from this unpaginated web text. Description and original locator are blank; no outcome, predictor, sample or model is supplied. No assignment by row order or numeric resemblance. Candidate Ns only for parent field-scope review: Table 2 college attendance N=7,838 participants; Table 3 college attendance n=3,062 participants age 15+ in 1997; Table 5 four-year dropout n=2,605 individuals contributing 96,871 person-month observations. Method also gives 1,962 two-year college respondents. Enrollment analysis excludes marriage/pregnancy before leaving high school and requires an interview after high school; persistence excludes marriage, birth or cohabitation at first enrollment; Table 3 additionally restricts to respondents age 15+ in 1997 for college-expectations eligibility. Missing independent variables are multiply imputed. No model is uniquely assigned, so none of these is promoted to target analytic N. No sum and no inference from df. Illustrative focal candidates, not an exhaustive list of predictors: Table 5 four-year dropout fertility-expectations OR 1.04 in Model 1 (B 0.04, SE 0.02, p < .05), OR 1.03 in Model 2 (B 0.03, SE 0.02, p < .05), and OR 1.03 in Models 3 and 4 (B 0.03, SE 0.02, no star; numeric p not established). Pregnancy OR 2.13 in Model 2 (B 0.75, SE 0.14, p < .001), OR 1.67 in Model 3 (B 0.51, SE 0.15, p < .001), and OR 2.09 in Model 4 (B 0.74, SE 0.17, p < .001). Model 4 male × (partner) pregnancy OR 0.46 (B −0.78, SE 0.31, p < .05). Table explicitly defines OR as odds ratio. Narrative separately prints 2.12 for pregnancy while Table 5 prints 2.13; these are separate reports, not reconciled or converted here. Other predictors also have ORs; two-year dropout analysis is described as results not shown. Metric alone cannot select a predictor, sample or model.
